Subject: Re: Draft SOW + pricing — follow up on price protections

Hi Logan —

Thanks for the draft SOW and the pricing grid. Procurement asked me to confirm a couple of items before we move to legal:

1) Price lock: Sunrise needs a 12-month firm price on the per-token rates tied to the committed tier we discussed.
2) MFN: we are requesting an MFN clause so Sunrise will receive any lower rate you make available to other customers of similar scale.
3) CPI cap: we want any annual indexation to be capped at 3% (CPI-U).

Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept those three points, and if not, what tradeoffs you’d propose (e.g., longer commit, higher minimum, or limited MFN scope)? Also attaching our redlines for convenience.

Appreciate a short summary we can include with our legal submission.

Best,

Hi Alyssa —

Thanks — and appreciate the clear asks. Short answers up front, then specifics below.

Summary (high level):
- Price lock: we can offer a 12-month price lock on per-token rates if Sunrise commits to a 12-month minimum spend (commit tier A).
- MFN: we can offer a limited MFN that applies to published base rates for the same customer class; excludes temporary promotional discounts, marketplace promos, and enterprise-only negotiated programs.
- CPI cap: we can cap indexation at CPI-U + 0.5% with an absolute annual cap of 2.5% (we are proposing this instead of 3%).

Details and tradeoffs:
1) Commit tiers and what they buy you
- Commit A (12-month): $120k/month commit (~est. 1.8B tokens/year) -> 12-month price lock, 10% off public hosted per-token list.
- Commit B (24-month): $85k/month commit (~est. 2.5B tokens/year) -> 18-month price lock + deeper discount, eligibility for smaller MFN scope and reduced audit frequency.

2) MFN scope
- We will grant MFN relative to published list pricing for customers in the same tier class (annual committed spend within ±20%). MFN will not apply to: one-off promotional credits, non-public marketplace pricing, or legacy custom deals with fundamentally different SLAs. This protects your economics while allowing us commercial flexibility.

3) CPI / indexation approach
- Rather than an unconditional 3% CPI cap, we propose CPI-U + 0.5%, not exceeding 2.5% per year. This balances predictable inflation protection for you and predictable margin for us. If Sunrise opts for a longer commit (24 months), we can drop the +0.5% step (i.e., cap at 2.0%).

4) Audit and transparency
- We will agree to quarterly usage reports and one annual usage audit right. Any MFN claims will be resolved with Red/Blue team mediation; if needed, each party bears its own audit costs unless material discrepancy (>3%) is found.

I’m looping in Marissa (SE) and Sean (Finance) to confirm the numbers and to attach the updated pricing grid so you can share with legal. If this is directionally acceptable I can send a redline that reflects the language changes.

Best,
Logan Wright
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Internal note —

Quick calc based on Alyssa’s ask and our models: if Sunrise signs Commit A (12m at $120k/mo) the blended margin stays ~32% after expected infra egress and support overhead. Commit B (24m, $85k/mo) improves margin ~45% thanks to capacity planning. MFN limited to published list pricing keeps our ability to run short-term promos.

Rishi: can you take a first pass on MFN language that matches Logan’s notes (published list only, carve out promo/marketplace)? Also need a concise CPI clause draft to give Alyssa — two options: 12m commit (cap 2.5%) or 24m commit (cap 2.0%).

Marissa
Principal SE, Redwood Inference

Team —

Draft MFN clause (TO SEND to Sunrise):
"Sunrise shall be entitled to any lower published per-token list price or published discount level that Redwood makes generally available to customers of the same committed spend class (±20% of Sunrise’s committed annual spend). Excluded from MFN are limited-time promotional offers, non-public marketplace pricing, or bespoke commercial arrangements tied to materially different SLA or support commitments."

CPI clause options (pick one):
Option 1 (12-month commit): "Prices shall remain fixed for the first 12 months following Effective Date. Thereafter, Redwood may increase prices annually based on the U.S. CPI-U index plus 0.5 percentage points, not to exceed 2.5% in any calendar year."
Option 2 (24-month commit): "Prices shall remain fixed for the first 18 months following Effective Date. Thereafter, Redwood may increase prices annually based on the U.S. CPI-U index, not to exceed 2.0% in any calendar year."

Notes: the MFN language tries to be narrow and measurable; the CPI options give Sunrise an explicit cap. If Sunrise insists on a pure 0% nominal increase for 12 months we should push for a higher commit or an escalated minimum spend.

Rishi
Associate General Counsel

Logan —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the options. Two quick clarifications from our side before we send to legal:
1) MFN carveouts: we understand promotional carveouts, but we need MFN to capture any lower list prices for customers with the same SLA (support and uptime). The ±20% committed spend bucket is acceptable if you can confirm it’s based on committed spend only (not actual usage).
2) CPI calculation: Sunrise prefers Option 1 with the 2.5% cap, but would like an explicit example in the contract showing how the cap is applied if CPI-U is 2% in a year (does Redwood apply 2%+0.5%=2.5% or capped at 2.5%?).

If you can send a word redline with the MFN and CPI text and confirm whether MFN reference is to committed spend, we’ll move to legal.

Best,
Alyssa

Alyssa, Tom —

Thanks — attaching the redline with the two CPI options and the MFN language that references committed spend explicitly. To answer your example directly: if CPI-U is 2.0% in a year, under Option 1 we would apply 2.0% + 0.5% = 2.5%, which equals the cap in that case. The contract language will state that the increase applied will be the lesser of (CPI-U + 0.5%) and 2.5%.

MFN confirmation: the MFN measurement will be against other customers’ committed spend levels (contractually documented committed spend), not actual realized usage. That is, the comparator is the committed tier in a signed contract.

Next steps:
- I attached the redline (Sunrise_RateProtections_Redline_v2.docx) with the MFN and both CPI clause options and called out the commit tiers.
- If Sunrise is good with Option 1 (12-month fixed then CPI-U +0.5% capped at 2.5%), we’ll prepare a version for signature and coordinate DocuSign.

I’ll follow up with Sean and finance to ensure billing setup aligns with committed reporting cadence. Happy to hop on a 20-minute call if you want to walk legal through the exact wording.

Cheers,
Logan Wright
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
